title: Chrysophanol Attenuates Glucocorticoid-Induced Osteoporosis by Targeting the E74-Like Factor 5/Osteoglycin-Regulated PI3K/AKT/mTOR Signaling Axis: An In Vitro and In Vivo Study.
authors: Chen, Rongjin; Yang, Chenhui; Chen, Changshun; Yang, Fei; Xiao, Hefang; Yang, Ao; Peng, Bo; Geng, Bin; Xia, Yayi
one_liner_zh: 该研究聚焦糖皮质激素性骨质疏松中ELF5转录因子对OGN的调控及药物分子对接，虽涉及TF-DNA调控和分子对接，但核心是疾病机制与药物筛选，非TF-DNA互作建模研究。
abstract: Glucocorticoid-induced osteoporosis (GIOP) is the most common form of secondary osteoporosis, characterized by severe impairment of osteoblast function and increased bone fragility. Current therapeutic options inadequately address glucocorticoid (GC)-induced osteoblast apoptosis and suppress osteogenesis, highlighting the need for novel targeted interventions. To explore the molecular pathogenesis of GIOP and identify therapeutic targets, we performed integrated transcriptomic analysis, bioinformatics approaches, and multiple experimental validation methods. We demonstrate that dexamethasone (DEX), a prototypical GC, robustly upregulates osteoglycin (OGN) expression in both cellular and animal models. Crucially, the transcription factor ELF5 functions as a critical transcriptional repressor of OGN, counteracting DEX effects. ELF5-mediated OGN repression is essential for maintaining pro-survival PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling integrity in osteoblasts. Molecular docking confirmed stable, high-affinity binding between the natural compound chrysophanol and OGN. Functionally, chrysophanol effectively antagonized DEX-induced OGN elevation and mitigated osteoblast apoptosis. This work is the first to define a role for the DEX-OGN-ELF5 axis in PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling as critical for osteoblast survival in GIOP. Chrysophanol, as a novel natural compound targeting this OGN-centric axis, presents a promising and potentially safer therapeutic alternative to bisphosphonates, which are associated with risks like atypical femoral fractures and osteonecrosis of the jaw. Our findings offer novel insights into the molecular pathogenesis of GIOP, identify a potential druggable ELF5/OGN/PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling axis, and establish a basis for future translational research in GC-induced bone diseases.
abstract_zh: 糖皮质激素诱导的骨质疏松症（GIOP）是继发性骨质疏松症最常见的形式，其特征为成骨细胞功能严重受损及骨脆性增加。当前治疗方案未能充分解决糖皮质激素（GC）诱导的成骨细胞凋亡并抑制骨生成，凸显了对新型靶向干预措施的需求。为探索GIOP的分子发病机制并识别治疗靶点，我们进行了整合转录组分析、生物信息学方法及多种实验验证手段。我们证明，地塞米松（DEX）作为典型GC，在细胞和动物模型中均显著上调骨甘氨酸（OGN）表达。关键的是，转录因子ELF5作为OGN的关键转录抑制因子，拮抗DEX效应。ELF5介导的OGN抑制对维持成骨细胞中促生存的PI3K/AKT/mTOR信号完整性至关重要。分子对接确认了天然化合物大黄酚与OGN之间的稳定高亲和力结合。功能上，大黄酚有效拮抗DEX诱导的OGN升高并减轻成骨细胞凋亡。本研究首次定义了DEX-OGN-ELF5轴在PI3K/AKT/mTOR信号中作为GIOP成骨细胞存活关键的作用。大黄酚作为靶向这一以OGN为中心的轴的新型天然化合物，为双膦酸盐类药物（其与不典型股骨骨折和颌骨坏死等风险相关）提供了一种有前景且可能更安全的治疗替代方案。我们的发现为GIOP的分子发病机制提供了新见解，识别了潜在的药物靶向ELF5/OGN/PI3K/AKT/mTOR信号轴，并为未来GC诱导骨疾病的转化研究奠定了基础。
